A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FS-DFM research and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–E. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable matching of their equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material.

before.justification: v2 reports original FS-DFM language-model evaluations, component ablations, checkerboard simulations, and generated-text examples in Section 5 and Appendices B and E.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments and qualitative outputs, with revised numerical entries in Appendix Table 5.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the same step-size conditioning, RK-2/RK-4 shortcut teachers, EMA updates, training losses, cumulative scalar, and CTMC sampling procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use FineWeb-Edu training and WikiText-103 evaluation, retaining unconditional generation, prefix continuation, corruption–recovery, and the synthetic checkerboard scenario. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments: DFM, Dream and LLaDA variants, SDTT, HDLM, MDLM–OWT, SEDD, and ReMDM variants are retained. Table 5 changes their scores without adding or removing comparison methods.

E3.justification: The reported preprocessing, model sizes, training budgets, sampling budgets, metrics, and 512-token-prefix/512-token-continuation protocol remain unchanged. No protocol revision is documented to accompany Table 5's entropy changes.

E4.justification: The cumulative-scalar, teacher-order, step-size-weight, and source-distribution ablations are unchanged, as are the checkerboard demonstration, training-time analysis, corruption–recovery examples, and generation trajectories.

E5.justification: Both retain the same averaging and descriptive median reporting. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seed statistics, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the revised entropy scores are evaluation results, not new statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 5 revises entropy values for SDTT, HDLM, MDLM–OWT, SEDD, and ReMDM: for example, SDTT (1 round) changes from 5.80 to 8.38 and MDLM–OWT from 5.90 to 8.47, reversing their ordering against unchanged FS-DFM entropies of 7.29–7.61. The two Training Data entries, (PPL 14.8, entropy 5.44) and (14.7, 7.70), become one containing (14.7, 7.70). These revisions are confined to supplementary entropy/reference results; model perplexities and the remaining results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, CTMC assumptions, Proposition A.1, Kolmogorov equations, cumulative-scalar derivation, and sampling mathematics in Sections 3–4 and Appendices A–B are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims, including matching a similar-size 1024-step DFM baseline with eight steps for 1024-token generation and up to 128-fold sampling acceleration.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations, result interpretations, and Appendix D's applicability limits and future directions are unchanged. Appendix E.3 retains its interpretation despite the revised entropy values.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains identical architecture, conditioning, optimizer, learning-rate, batch-size, training-duration, and hardware disclosures. Code-access information and model-release statements are also unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to prior diffusion, flow-matching, and distillation methods are unchanged. Bibliography entries move with pagination; the new acknowledgements do not introduce research references.

P1.justification: v5 updates the date/version text and adds an acknowledgement to Ruixiang Zhang after the conclusion and another in Appendix E.5. The scientific prose, terminology, and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 5 loses the additional Training Data row, slightly shortening its structure. Acknowledgements produce local text and bibliography reflow. Figures, captions, axes, and the other table structures are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Consolidating Table 5's differently valued Training Data rows improves clarity. However, the substantive revision raises baseline entropies and changes their ordering against FS-DFM without explaining the calculation or correction; the metric description remains unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether these revisions improve measurement reliability, so the small presentation benefit does not establish a reliable net improvement in paper quality.
